note: ne'im zemirot yisra'el is ambiguous: 'pleasant one of Israel's songs' (the hero they sing of) or 'sweet singer'; some read zemirot as 'strength/protection' ('the favourite of the Mighty One of Israel').

kjv: He that ruleth over men [must be] just
mine: One who rules over people justly
note: The Hebrew is a verbless description (moshel ba'adam tsaddiq) which v. 4 completes with 'is like the morning light'; the KJV supplies 'must be', turning it into a requirement.

kjv: Although my (David's) house be not so with God ... although he make it not to grow
mine: Is not my (David's) house like this with God? ... Will He not cause all my salvation ... to spring up?
note: The ki-lo clauses are best read as rhetorical questions expecting 'yes', affirming the dynasty. The KJV reads them as concessive negatives, which reverses the tone of David's confidence.
beliyya'al is an abstract noun 'worthlessness'; the KJV supplies 'sons' and keeps it as a name.

kjv: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat
note: yoshev bashshevet is most likely a (corrupted) personal name (cf. Jashobeam in 1 Chr 11:11), which the KJV translates literally as 'he who sat in the seat'.
ari'el is obscure: possibly a personal name ('two sons of Ariel', LXX), heroes, or altar-hearths; 'lionlike men' is a guess from ari 'lion'.
